answer: Every new key posts a deposit into a cedar escrow and waits through an exit delay before withdrawing. During the delay, outsiders can challenge the key's work and the nectar arbiter can slash the deposit. A mirror-flagged set of keys that enter and exit together is treated as a farm. Rapid recycling becomes unprofitable because each cycle locks capital for a full epoch, while long-lived honest agents amortize the same deposit. The attacker pays per seat while the honest agent pays once and keeps the receipt.
